spec.title: Lens: shared clients and background agent communication

status.comment: Owner-authorized headless communication foundation. Quicklens UI and full ZAP control are subsequent layers, not implied by a broker acknowledgement.

p.packaging: The package is org.vibevm.zap/lens, with npm identity @org.vibevm.zap/lens. Quicklens, gamelens and codlens are separate entry points sharing the same protocol, client model, domain adapter and reusable components. Browser, Electron main/preload and Node broker have explicit import and build boundaries. The planning engine is the separate org.vibevm.zap/zap package, accessed through its public interface. Product runtime code has no dependency on host Vibevm source-tree paths; repository extraction remains deferred.

p.replanning: Ordinary agent chat and lens controls can both initiate plan changes during execution through the same domain operations. A proposal records its base plan revision and relevant specification digest. New or changed specifications trigger reassessment through change signals and authoritative digest checks at preparation/admission boundaries. Specification text is input, not authority. Stale previews refuse application. Affected in-flight results retain their original basis and require reconciliation; unaffected work may continue. Existing scoped textual authorization does not require a duplicate graphical approval. This domain behavior must not be claimed implemented by the initial communication broker.

p.protocol: The application protocol is lens/1 and is independent of MCP transport revision. Runtime schemas validate unknown external data; semantic identifiers are distinct types. Broker-issued message IDs, stable principal/actor/client-request idempotency, correlation and causation IDs, and lossless sequence/revision representations survive reconnect. Incompatible versions and malformed or oversized payloads return typed errors.

p.broker: One user-local broker serves several lens clients and many simultaneous actors/conversations. Transactional persistence commits actionable messages, questions, answers, bindings, deliveries and event positions before acknowledging them. The broker remains independent of a renderer lifetime and has no global current question or current agent. Restart restores durable state; bounded paging/backpressure never silently discards an unanswered question or answer.

p.nonblocking: Publishing a question returns its durable ID promptly and never waits for a human response. Model-facing inbox reads default to no wait. Background subscriptions and host adapters wait outside the normal agent tool request. The ordinary CLI/desktop text flow remains usable; input injection into unrelated or unowned terminals, visible desktop prompt manipulation and transcript rewriting are prohibited. PROP-006 separately permits visible, authorized input through an explicitly owned managed-agent virtual terminal with an exclusive input-control lease.

p.identity: Authenticated principals, durable actor identities and transient bindings are separate. Create and resume are different operations. Resume proves ownership, atomically advances the binding generation and fences stale writers/receivers. An actor can delegate only a subset of its authorized workspace/conversation capabilities. MCP client/session metadata, native display names and parent claims alone are not authentication. Subagents have explicit addressed inboxes, including nested and concurrent cases; ambiguous native identity must not route to another actor.

p.questions: An open question has an exact revision. Answer, cancel and expiry compete transactionally; one transition wins. A duplicate identical request returns its original result, while a conflicting second answer refuses. A separate authorized amendment retains earlier answers and emits a new event. Expired/cancelled questions cannot be answered silently. The original requester and reply policy remain explicit when a completed child's reply is forwarded to its parent.

p.delivery: Delivery identity is per message and logical recipient, with separate attempts bound to adapter generation. Persisted, offered, host-accepted, actor-acknowledged and answered are distinct observations; missing observation is not failure or success. At-least-once delivery uses idempotent sparse acknowledgements. A stream cursor resumes observation and never acknowledges inbox contents. Gaps require explicit resynchronization. A lost host response remains uncertain until reconciled, without blindly repeating a command.

p.transport: The initial host transport uses bounded HTTP commands and an SSE event stream on loopback, with validated Host/Origin and scoped authentication for reads, writes and streams. The MCP bridge uses an official SDK and immediate-return tools; it does not pretend that generic MCP logging/resource notifications enter a model's context. CLI commands provide a headless lens fixture over the same broker semantics. Logs exclude credential material and raw private payloads by default.

p.adapters: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and Qwen Code use separate capability-aware adapters. Native hooks, channels or server APIs may deliver at safe points or wake a supported idle session. Existing ordinary sessions are not claimed attachable without a verified binding. Busy/idle races, host rejection, unsupported Windows peer transports and unknown consumption are explicit. Captured/synthetic adapter tests are distinguished from live host inference. Host adapters cannot forge broker or human acknowledgement.

p.authority: Agent, viewer, human responder, human plan approver and trusted execution adapter have distinct scoped capabilities. An agent can request a preview or propose intent but cannot self-assert human authority. Existing scoped Owner authority may permit routine changes without an additional human approval. Where ZAP requires a fresh plan approval, it binds the authenticated human, exact preview digest, store/campaign/base/revision, action/operation identity and expiry, and is consumed once for that operation. ZAP retains its actual credentials, economics, holds, admission and reconciliation. A communication-stage implementation must truthfully refuse unimplemented plan execution.

p.verification: Acceptance includes runtime validation/type checks, real Node protocol tests, an actual official-SDK MCP round trip, simultaneous parent/nested-child questions and out-of-order lens answers, duplicate/restart/stale-binding/wrong-scope/answer-race/retention-gap cases, and proof that human waits leave tool calls completed. Host capability claims require documented version/OS evidence and live results where claimed. Coding workers use gpt-5.6-luna/high; isolated live protocol actors may use Owner-authorized weak/free models with short bounded prompts. No uncontrolled model polling, paid-provider fallback or local Qwen-model inference is implied.
